### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via manager_id (literal, a string literal in linkDemoStaffManagers), /api/v1/auth/admin/set-user-manager (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/capabilities/approvals.mdx`  _(via manager_id (literal, a string literal in linkDemoStaffManagers), /api/v1/auth/admin/set-user-manager (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx`  _(via manager_id (literal, a string literal in linkDemoStaffManagers))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via manager_id (literal, a string literal in linkDemoStaffManagers), /api/v1/auth/admin/set-user-manager (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **152** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a485b5a3e28d84550e8a33bbb5cfc2d52c82ff9e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9c21e4dc9054fe1a95c93336c58a51f24d1b8efc` — the merge of head `53d29e263c2573b2442cd17af01eedab1e2c8d4b` into base `a485b5a3e28d84550e8a33bbb5cfc2d52c82ff9e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9c21e4dc9054fe1a95c93336c58a51f24d1b8efc && git checkout 9c21e4dc9054fe1a95c93336c58a51f24d1b8efc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a485b5a3e28d84550e8a33bbb5cfc2d52c82ff9e 53d29e263c2573b2442cd17af01eedab1e2c8d4b && git checkout -B drift-repro a485b5a3e28d84550e8a33bbb5cfc2d52c82ff9e && git merge --no-ff 53d29e263c2573b2442cd17af01eedab1e2c8d4b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a485b5a3e28d84550e8a33bbb5cfc2d52c82ff9e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a485b5a3e28d84550e8a33bbb5cfc2d52c82ff9e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a516ef70932a183ab3d4b04336ebef8381655a2b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/demo-staff.zod.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/demo-staff.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-set-user-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/alias-probe.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs

Inputs read: card #26616 (body, the re-lane note, the triage grade, the claim, the os-dev-report); PR #26763 body and file list; the net diff `43731031..a516ef70` (11 files, +513/−9); the check-runs on the head. The PR body's account was read and then set aside; every judgment below is on the tree.

Gate verdicts on the head (check-run conclusions, read 2026-10-27 at the time of this record): green — `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Type Check · source gates` (the lane carrying `check:authorable-surface` and `check:docs`), `Lint · ESLint` (carrying `check:engine-double-contract`), `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Test UI`, `Build Docs`, `Build UI Deps`, `Check PR Size`. Still `in_progress` when this record was closed: `Test Core (1–8/8)`, `Build Core`, `Type Check · consumer gates` (carries `check:api-surface`), `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI`. The verdict below is on the tree; the seat posts it only once those required lanes report `success`, and a red there re-opens this record rather than being adopted.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set, `DemoStaffSchema`** (`demo-staff.zod.ts`): one new optional key `manager: z.string().email()`. A key the strict shape refused is now accepted; nothing accepted before is refused now (a `manager`-less list parses as it did). ⇒ `Metadata-protocol: added`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. Right.
- **Aliases** `managerEmail`, `managerId`, `reportsTo`, `supervisor` → `manager`: each filed key is one the shape rejects and each target is one it accepts (the alias-integrity claims hold). `aliasProbe` (`alias-probe.ts:21`) lowercases and strips `_ - space`, so `manager_id`, `manager_email`, `reports_to` reach the same entries; the `manager_id` row that shared `managerId`'s probe was rightly dropped in `8e1dde38` rather than kept as a dead second spelling. Right.
- **Stack check** (`stack.zod.ts`): `collectDemoStaffManagerErrors` is called from `collectDemoStaffErrors`, which `validateCrossReferences` runs BEFORE its `objectNames.size === 0` early return, and `defineStack` runs `validateCrossReferences` unconditionally in strict mode (the default) on the parsed `result.data`. Nothing conditions it; the only skip is `strict: false`, which skips every cross-reference check and predates this PR. "At load, never silently skipped" holds for `defineStack`, `os validate`, `os build` and every host config. Right.
- **Error code**: `STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID` is an existing ledger row (`error-code-ledger.zod.ts:1576`, "items name objects the stack does not define" plus the aggregate's other findings); the class `StackCrossReferenceError extends StackRefusalError` carries 422. A `manager` naming no entry is exactly a stack-level reference the stack does not define; self-reference and loops ride the same aggregate the duplicate-name and duplicate-address findings already ride. Right, and no new code was minted outside the ledger.
- **Compose**: `COMPOSE_KEY_DISPOSITIONS.demoStaff = 'concat'`; `composeStacks` refuses an input not built by `defineStack`, and `collectArtifactCrossReferenceErrors` does not re-judge managers on the composed list — so a manager resolves within the list its own `defineStack` saw, and a cross-publisher manager is refused at its input. Matches the card ("another entry" of the same list) and the acceptance note. Right.
- **Identity key = email, folded the same way on both sides**: the stack check keys `indicesByEmail` on `email.trim().toLowerCase()` and looks `manager.trim().toLowerCase()` up in it; the provisioning folds `entry.manager` the same way and resolves it through `findUserIdByEmail` → `addressSpellings([lowercased])`, the same read the first pass used to find or create every account — so if the first pass found the manager's account the second pass finds it by construction. `.email()` refuses whitespace, so `trim()` is inert; `toLowerCase()` is the fold the duplicate-address refusal and sign-up storage already use. Choosing the address over the card's "by name or email" is right: `name` is a Tier-1 self-editable label and is the SEED's key, not the account's. Right.
- **Public surface, plugin-auth**: `DemoStaffOutcome` gains `managersLinked` and `managersKept` (required, readonly); the only producer is `provisionDemoStaff`, so for every reader it is a widening. Right.
- **Generated artifacts**: `authorable-surface/system.json` (+`system/DemoStaff:manager`, in sorted position) and `content/docs/references/system/demo-staff.mdx` (+1 row in schema key order) are generator outputs; the lane that runs `check:authorable-surface` and `check:docs` is `Type Check · source gates`, green on this head, so they are certified regenerated, not taken on the body's word. `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` `pinned: 1 → 2` for `demo-staff.test.ts` is the `check:engine-double-contract --write` output for the second `update` double the new tests add; that gate runs in `Lint · ESLint`, green. A pinned count growing is coverage growth, the ledger's ordinary direction.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/26616-demo-staff-manager.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth: minor`. The kind is `added`, and a kind takes at least `minor` on every package the diff moves (Post-Task Checklist step 3); both packages move. Both declaration lines are present in the PR body and in the changeset body: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added`. Not breaking, so no ADR-0087 marker is owed. `Check Changeset` green. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []` — none to answer.
- **Out-of-scope finding 1 (depth cap not checked at load)**: the dev's note says a chain longer than 20 "is refused by the set-manager write at the boot and reported, never skipped". Read against `walkChain` that is only true for SOME declaration orders: the walk goes UPWARD from the proposed manager, so a chain declared subordinate-first (E1→E2, E2→E3, …) is written link by link, each walk seeing only the short chain above, and a 21-link chain lands unrefused; declared top-first it is refused at the last write. No file in `hits` claims the cap (the TSDoc names three refusals only), so it is not a declared≠enforced defect of this diff; it is a wrong sentence in the acceptance note. **Should-fix**: correct the note (or carry the cap into the load-time walk, which already has the path length, once `MAX_MANAGER_CHAIN_DEPTH` has a home in spec — a card, not this PR).
- **Out-of-scope finding 2 / `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — FILES`**: under ruling #26369 B that value is a permitted form; the seat files the owed card and rewrites the line to `#N` before ACCEPT (pm-dispatch SKILL.md:313, review-checklist.md:18) — a seat act, not a contract-review verdict. The zero-headroom claim is TRUE on this head: `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md` is 24005 bytes, priced 23985 → 5997 tokens = its ceiling; `evals/config-plugins-ops.json` is 5873 bytes → 1469 = its ceiling. One correction to the note: "raising a ceiling is not this card's call" is half right — the standing ruling 「A:先削重复,余额按实测提高」 (card #26302, same row) is the payment path, so the follow-up card should cite it and pay in that order (cut restatements first, then raise AT the measurement). Deferral acceptable.
- **Attribution at boot**: `authSystemWriteContext()` with no request resolves no `attributedUserId` and answers `{ isSystem: true }` — the same system write the first pass's `email_verified` update is. Right.
- **Hand-cleared manager re-written**: consistent with the module's existing idempotency, where a hand-removed position or permission-set assignment is also re-added ("only its missing assignments are added"); the declaration wins over absence only, the boot is development-only, and the count is logged. Acceptable; see ④ should-fix on the schema TSDoc.
- Governed surfaces: none in the file list; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` green; 522 changed lines. Premise (a `demoStaff` entry carries `name`, `email`, `position?`, `permissionSets?` only) holds on `43731031`.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/demo-staff.zod.ts` — holds.**
- Tried: a manager written as a display name → refused at `demoStaff.N.manager` by `.email()` with a message that names the fix. A manager written as a user id via `managerId: 'usr_…'` → alias to `manager`, then `.email()` refuses the id, two loud steps, no silent strip. Mixed-case address → accepted here, folded in the stack check and the provisioning identically (①).
- **Should-fix (docs, one clause)**: the key's TSDoc says "A manager someone already set on that account is left as it is" but not that a CLEARED one is written again — the one case an operator can be surprised by. The module header and the changeset say it; the authorable TSDoc, which an IDE shows the author, does not. Add the clause there (the `describe` and the mdx row need not change).

**`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` — holds.**
- Cycle detection is complete for this graph: out-degree is at most one (one `manager` per entry), so from any unsettled start the walk either reaches an entry with no manager, a settled entry, or revisits the current path. A revisit is a loop, reported once with `path.slice(indexOf(cursor))` (the tail an entry hangs from is excluded, as the test pins); every entry on the path is then settled, so a later start reaching the same loop stops at a settled node and does not report it twice; a second, disjoint loop is found from its own unsettled start; a long loop is only a longer path. A self-reference is diverted to its own refusal before `managerOf.set`, so a self-loop never enters the walk. Tried the duplicate-address edge: an entry whose own `email` is a repeat and that names that address resolves to the FIRST occurrence (`?.[0]`), so it is reported as a link beside the duplicate-address refusal rather than as self-reference — both loud, acceptable.
- Runs at load, unconditionally, in strict `defineStack`; status 422 under an existing ledger code (①). Messages carry no tracker number (the `check:doc-authoring` rule) and each names the remedy.
- The `manager`-is-not-a-string skip is moot: in strict mode the check reads the parsed `result.data`, where `manager` is already a valid address.

**Cited code, read to judge the above (not reviewed; for the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`):**
- `demo-staff.ts`: the second pass runs after the first pass's loop, inside the same `provisionDemoStaff` call, on the same `kernel:ready` hook, and `AppPlugin` seeds at `kernel:bootstrapped` — so "after every entry exists, before the seed" holds. Each entry is its own `try/catch`; a thrown `find`/`update` or a refusal is pushed to `outcome.failed` and `auth-plugin.ts` logs every `failed` row at `warn` — it cannot fail half-way in silence. The refusals (self, cycle, depth, cross-org, directory-owned) are `applyUserManagerLink`'s own; the module carries no copy.
- **Should-fix (lane)**: `linkDeps` passes no `logger`, so `membershipOrgIds`'s "the cross-organization screen could not read sys_member, so the link was accepted without it" warning is dropped on this path — the one degradation that module promises to say once is silent here. Pass `ctx.logger` through `DemoStaffProvisioningDeps`. Not a must-fix: the fail-open posture is the endpoint's own and the read's failure at boot is improbable.

Must-fixes: none. Should-fixes: three (the schema TSDoc clause; the depth-cap sentence in the acceptance note; the dropped logger on `linkDeps`).

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · `domain:spec` seat 1 (#6017) · session `session_01WGufzfhobWEgUUrjz4rrbh` · 2026-10-27T15:51Z

Head `53d29e263c2573b2442cd17af01eedab1e2c8d4b`. Card #26616, claim `6442804755`, dev report `6445286003`.

- **Contract review:** owed at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER for `system/demo-staff.zod.ts` and `stack.zod.ts`. PASS `6445518048` at `a516ef70`, with no must-fixes. The one commit since then, `53d29e26`, lands should-fixes (a) and (c) only: the diff from `a516ef70` to `53d29e26` is 4 files, +39/−4.
  - (a) The `manager` TSDoc now says that a cleared manager is written again on the next boot.
  - (c) `DemoStaffProvisioningDeps.logger` is passed into `linkDeps` (auth-plugin passes `ctx.logger`). A new unit case makes `sys_member` unreachable and pins that the warning lands once while the link is still written.
- **(b):** the PR body's depth-cap note now says what the tree does. A declared chain is bounded only when written top-first. The same order hole in `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/set-user-manager` predates this PR and is filed as #26775 (`domain:server`).
- **Lane seat (rest of the diff, TIER_DEFAULT):**
  - `manager` names another entry by email, folded with `trim().toLowerCase()` on both the stack and the provisioning side.
  - The stack refuses a manager that names no entry, a self-reference and a loop with `STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID` (422), at load.
  - The second provisioning pass runs after every entry exists, through `applyUserManagerLink`. It writes only a null `manager_id`, and each entry fails loudly to `warn`.
  - No example app declares `demoStaff`.
- **Skills-docs:** `#26764`. Both skills files are at zero headroom, and the card cites the #26302 payment path.
- **Shape:** `Fixes #26616`, 11 files. `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/plugin-auth` are minor. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added`. `check-governed-merges --pr 26763`: NOT governed, 557 changed lines.
- **Gates:** check-runs on this head are 42 success, 9 skipped and 0 red. `mergeable_state` is clean.
- **Landing:** Tier S. `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` in this act.
